title: The frozen pizza market after the price of cheese rises
scenario: Cheese is an input in making frozen pizza, and its price rises sharply.

stimulus.title: The frozen pizza market at the old price
stimulus.html:
Weekly quantities in an invented country's market for frozen pizza at the original equilibrium price of $6, after the price of cheese rises
Price per pizzaQuantity demanded (pizzas per week)Quantity supplied (pizzas per week)
$6500350

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the market for frozen pizza and show the effect of the rise in the price of cheese. Label the new equilibrium price P2 and the new equilibrium quantity Q2.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled graph: Price on the vertical axis, Quantity on the horizontal axis, and labeled demand and supply curves
accept: P and Q on the axes
D and S on the curves

rubric.point: The supply curve shifted to the left (S1 to S2)
accept: a leftward shift of supply with an arrow

rubric.point: A new equilibrium where D meets S2, with P2 higher than P1 and Q2 lower than Q1
accept: the new price and quantity marked on the axes, P2 above P1 and Q2 below Q1

parts.sample: Price is on the vertical axis and Quantity on the horizontal axis. D slopes down and S1 slopes up, crossing at P1 and Q1. The rise in the price of cheese raises the cost of making each pizza, so supply shifts left to S2 (arrow from S1 to S2). S2 meets D at a higher price, P2, and a smaller quantity, Q2, both marked with dashed lines to the axes.

key.because: a rise in the price of cheese, an input

slips.D: Cheese is an input for pizza makers, so its price shifts supply; buyers' wants have not changed.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Use the data in the table. Calculate the shortage at the original price of $6 after the price of cheese rises. Show your work.

rubric.point: 150 pizzas per week, with work shown (500 - 350)

parts.sample: Shortage = quantity demanded - quantity supplied = <math class="mac-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>500</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>350</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>150</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500 - 350 = 150</annotation></semantics></math> pizzas per week.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Explain how the shortage in part B moves the market to its new equilibrium.

rubric.point: The shortage pushes the price up, and as it rises the quantity demanded falls and the quantity supplied rises until they are equal at the new equilibrium
accept: buyers compete for the scarce pizzas, so the price is bid up until quantity demanded equals quantity supplied

parts.sample: At $6, buyers want 150 more pizzas than sellers offer, so buyers compete for the scarce pizzas and sellers raise their prices. As the price rises, the quantity demanded falls (a movement along D) and the quantity supplied rises (a movement along S2) until the two are equal at the new equilibrium price P2.
